claim: In the mammalian retina, inhibitory inputs onto starburst amacrine cells (SACs) are required for robust direction selectivity of On-Off direction-selective ganglion cells (On-Off DSGCs) against noisy backgrounds.
source: Previously, we found that in the mammalian retina, inhibitory inputs onto starburst amacrine cells (SACs) are required for robust direction selectivity of On-Off direction-selective ganglion cells (On-Off DSGCs) against noisy backgrounds (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Chen et al., 2016).

claim: When visual noise is present in the background, the motion-evoked inhibition to an On-Off DSGC is preserved by a disinhibitory motif consisting of a serially connected network of neighboring SACs presynaptic to the DSGC.
source: Here, we show that when visual noise is present in the background, the motion-evoked inhibition to an On-Off DSGC is preserved by a disinhibitory motif consisting of a serially connected network of neighboring SACs presynaptic to the DSGC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including voltage clamp recordings and paired recordings.

claim: The preservation of inhibition by a disinhibitory motif arises from the interaction between visually evoked network dynamics and short-term synaptic plasticity at the SAC-DSGC synapse.
source: This preservation of inhibition by a disinhibitory motif arises from the interaction between visually evoked network dynamics and short-term synaptic plasticity at the SAC-DSGC synapse.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing short-term depression at SAC-DSGC synapses and the effects of SAC activation patterns.

claim: Disinhibitory microcircuits are prominently involved in sensory processing, learning, and memory in the neocortex and the hippocampus.
source: Disinhibitory microcircuits are prominently involved in sensory processing, learning, and memory in the neocortex and the hippocampus (Jiang et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2013; Letzkus et al., 2011; Pfeffer et al., 2013; Pi et al., 2013), and in action selection in basal ganglia (reviewed in Chevalier and Deniau, 1990; Letzkus et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Disinhibitory microcircuits are involved in action selection in basal ganglia.
source: Disinhibitory microcircuits are prominently involved in sensory processing, learning, and memory in the neocortex and the hippocampus (Jiang et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2013; Letzkus et al., 2011; Pfeffer et al., 2013; Pi et al., 2013), and in action selection in basal ganglia (reviewed in Chevalier and Deniau, 1990; Letzkus et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: The functions of disinhibitory microcircuits in diverse brain circuits have so far been exclusively attributed to their disinhibitory influences on the principal neurons by relieving the principal neurons from ongoing inhibition.
source: Their functions in these diverse circuits have so far been exclusively attributed to their disinhibitory influences on the principal neurons by relieving the principal neurons from ongoing inhibition.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge about disinhibitory circuits.

claim: On-Off type DSGCs receive directional inhibition from starburst amacrine cells (SACs).
source: On-Off type DSGCs, a major type of retinal output neuron with directionally tuned spiking activity (Barlow and Levick, 1965), receive directional inhibition from starburst amacrine cells (SACs) (Briggman et al., 2011; Euler et al., 2002; Fried et al., 2005; Lee et al., 2010; Taylor and Vaney, 2002; Wei et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: SACs receive inhibitory inputs from neighboring SACs.
source: SACs themselves receive inhibitory inputs from neighboring SACs (Chen et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016; Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lee and Zhou, 2006) and wide-field amacrine cells (WACs) (Chen et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016; Huang et al., 2019), and therefore participate in WAC-SAC-DSGC and SAC-SAC-DSGC 'disinhibitory' motifs (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: SACs receive inhibitory inputs from wide-field amacrine cells (WACs).
source: SACs themselves receive inhibitory inputs from neighboring SACs (Chen et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016; Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lee and Zhou, 2006) and wide-field amacrine cells (WACs) (Chen et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016; Huang et al., 2019), and therefore participate in WAC-SAC-DSGC and SAC-SAC-DSGC 'disinhibitory' motifs (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In Gabra2 cKO mice, GABA-A receptor α2 subunit is selectively removed from SACs.
source: When both these motifs are disrupted in a conditional knockout mouse line in which GABA-A receptor a2 subunit is selectively removed from SACs (Gabra2 cKO) (Auferkorte et al., 2012; Figure 1d schematic), the direction selectivity of On-Off DSGCs is differentially affected in a visual stimulus-dependent manner (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research and genetic manipulation described in the manuscript.

claim: The responses of On-Off DSGCs to the leading edge of a bright moving bar (On responses) in Gabra2 cKO mice show normal direction selectivity when the bar moves against a homogeneous gray background.
source: The responses of On-Off DSGCs to the leading edge of a bright moving bar (On responses) in Gabra2 cKO mice show normal direction selectivity when the bar moves against a homogeneous gray background.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1c-e.

claim: When the bar moves against a 'noisy' background of a randomly flickering checkerboard, DSGC On responses in Gabra2 cKO mice show impaired direction selectivity.
source: However, when the bar moves against a 'noisy' background of a randomly flickering checkerboard, DSGC On responses show impaired direction selectivity (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and experimental data in Figure 1c-f.

claim: In the On pathway, inhibitory input to SACs is not required for the implementation of direction selectivity.
source: Therefore, in the On pathway, inhibitory input to SACs is not required for the implementation of direction selectivity, but is specifically required for the robustness of this selectivity when flickering noise is present in the motion background.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing normal direction selectivity in noise-free conditions in Gabra2 cKO mice.

claim: Inhibitory input to SACs is specifically required for the robustness of direction selectivity when flickering noise is present in the motion background.
source: Therefore, in the On pathway, inhibitory input to SACs is not required for the implementation of direction selectivity, but is specifically required for the robustness of this selectivity when flickering noise is present in the motion background.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing impaired direction selectivity in noisy conditions in Gabra2 cKO mice.

claim: The SAC-SAC-DSGC microcircuit is the motif that underlies the noise resilience of direction selectivity in the On pathway.
source: In this study, we identified the SAC-SAC-DSGC microcircuit as the motif that underlies the noise resilience of direction selectivity in the On pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing control, Gabra2 cKO, and Vgat cKO mice.

claim: The SAC-SAC-DSGC motif preserves motion-evoked DSGC inhibition in the noisy background.
source: Combining genetic, functional and computational modeling approaches, we found that instead of disinhibiting DSGCs, this motif preserves motion-evoked DSGC inhibition in the noisy background, thereby preserving the direction selectivity of the DSGC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from voltage clamp recordings and paired recordings.

claim: The inverted algorithm of the SAC-SAC-DSGC motif leverages the center-surround receptive field (RF) of SACs.
source: This unexpected, inverted algorithm leverages the center-surround receptive field (RF) of SACs, and results from the interaction between visual noise-generated network dynamics and short-term plasticity at the SAC-DSGC synapse.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing SAC surround suppression and computational modeling.

claim: The inverted algorithm results from the interaction between visual noise-generated network dynamics and short-term plasticity at the SAC-DSGC synapse.
source: This unexpected, inverted algorithm leverages the center-surround receptive field (RF) of SACs, and results from the interaction between visual noise-generated network dynamics and short-term plasticity at the SAC-DSGC synapse.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing short-term depression and the effects of SAC activation patterns.

claim: In Gabra2 cKO mice, GABAergic inputs to SACs are selectively eliminated while the rest of retinal inhibitory circuitry remains intact.
source: In Gabra2 cKO mice, GABAergic inputs to SACs are selectively eliminated while the rest of retinal inhibitory circuitry remains intact (Chen et al., 2016; Figure 1d schematic).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and genetic manipulation.

claim: When probed with a moving bar against a gray background, the direction selectivity of On-Off DSGC On spiking responses in Gabra2 cKO mice was not impaired compared to that in control mice.
source: When probed with a moving bar against a gray background, the direction selectivity of On-Off DSGC On spiking responses in Gabra2 cKO mice was not impaired compared to that in control mice (Chen et al., 2016; Figure 1c–e).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and experimental data shown in Figure 1c-e.

claim: When the background of the moving bar was a randomly flickering checkerboard, motion-evoked On spiking activity was increased in the null direction in Gabra2 cKO mice, resulting in reduced direction selectivity.
source: However, when the background of the moving bar was a randomly flickering checkerboard (see Materials and methods), motion-evoked On spiking activity was increased in the anti-preferred, or null direction, resulting in reduced direction selectivity as measured by the direction selectivity index (DSI) (Figure 1c–d and f, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c-d and f.

claim: The enhanced null-direction spiking triggered by the moving bar in the DSGCs of the Gabra2 cKO group was due to attenuated inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) of DSGCs.
source: The enhanced null-direction spiking triggered by the moving bar in the DSGCs of the Gabra2 cKO group was due to attenuated inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) of DSGCs (Figure 1g–j), which come from the GABAergic outputs of SACs (Briggman et al., 2011; Fried et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2010; Taylor and Vaney, 2002; Wei et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1g-j and citations to prior research.

claim: DSGC IPSCs come from the GABAergic outputs of SACs.
source: The enhanced null-direction spiking triggered by the moving bar in the DSGCs of the Gabra2 cKO group was due to attenuated inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) of DSGCs (Figure 1g–j), which come from the GABAergic outputs of SACs (Briggman et al., 2011; Fried et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2010; Taylor and Vaney, 2002; Wei et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In the baseline period before the onset of the moving bar, the flickering checkerboard-evoked DSGC IPSCs in the control and cKO groups had similar amplitudes.
source: But in the baseline period before the onset of the moving bar, the flickering checkerboard-evoked DSGC IPSCs in the control and cKO groups had similar amplitudes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) of the DSGC originate predominantly from glutamatergic bipolar cells during the noisy bar stimulus.
source: In addition, the excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) of the DSGC, which originate predominantly from glutamatergic bipolar cells during this noisy bar stimulus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), were not affected compared to the control group (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, also see Supplemental Discussion on the contributions of glutamatergic and cholinergic excitation to DSGC with noise-free and noisy backgrounds).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The EPSCs of the DSGC were not affected in Gabra2 cKO mice compared to the control group during the noisy bar stimulus.
source: In addition, the excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) of the DSGC, which originate predominantly from glutamatergic bipolar cells during this noisy bar stimulus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), were not affected compared to the control group (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, also see Supplemental Discussion on the contributions of glutamatergic and cholinergic excitation to DSGC with noise-free and noisy backgrounds).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: GABAergic inputs onto SACs are important for the noise resilience of DSGC direction selectivity by preserving the strength of directionally tuned inhibition from SACs to DSGCs during motion over a noisy background.
source: Therefore, GABAergic inputs onto SACs are important for the noise resilience of DSGC direction selectivity by preserving the strength of directionally tuned inhibition from SACs to DSGCs during motion over a noisy background.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing attenuated IPSCs in Gabra2 cKO mice.

claim: In control animals, the bar entering the SAC's RF surround with a noise-free background evoked a brief period of membrane hyperpolarization prior to the depolarizing response evoked by the bar crossing the RF center.
source: In control animals, the bar entering the SAC's RF surround with a noise-free background evoked a brief period of membrane hyperpolarization prior to the depolarizing response evoked by the bar crossing the RF center (Figure 2a, left trace).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Similar patterns of SAC surround suppression have been observed in the rabbit.
source: Similar patterns of SAC surround suppression have been observed in the rabbit (Lee and Zhou, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: In the presence of flickering noise, control SACs exhibited flicker-evoked membrane depolarization during the baseline period before the onset of motion.
source: In the presence of flickering noise, control SACs exhibited flicker-evoked membrane depolarization (termed 'flicker response') during the baseline period before the onset of motion (Figure 2a, right trace).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The flicker response of control SACs was transiently suppressed when the bar traveled across the RF surround, creating a 'silent', or noise-free period of SAC Vm immediately before motion-evoked depolarization.
source: This flicker response was transiently suppressed when the bar traveled across the RF surround, creating a 'silent', or noise-free period of SAC Vm immediately before motion-evoked depolarization caused by the bar moving in the RF center (Figure 2a, right trace).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: In Gabra2 cKO mice, SAC resting somatic membrane potentials and flicker responses during the baseline period were not affected compared to the controls.
source: In Gabra2 cKO mice, SAC resting somatic membrane potentials and flicker responses during the baseline period were not affected compared to the controls (Figure 2b, d and g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b, d and g.

claim: The SAC depolarization evoked by the bar traversing the RF center was not affected in Gabra2 cKO mice.
source: The SAC depolarization evoked by the bar traversing the RF center was also not affected in Gabra2 cKO mice (Figure 2f and i).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f and i.

claim: Moving bar-evoked surround suppression of SAC Vm was significantly impaired in Gabra2 cKO mice.
source: However, moving bar-evoked surround suppression of SAC Vm was significantly impaired.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the noise-free background, SACs in the Gabra2 cKO group exhibited reduced membrane hyperpolarization.
source: In the noise-free background, SACs in the Gabra2 cKO group exhibited reduced membrane hyperpolarization (Figure 2e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: In the noisy background, flicker responses of SACs were less effectively suppressed in the Gabra2 cKO group when the bar traversed the RF surround.
source: In the noisy background, flicker responses of SACs were less effectively suppressed in the cKO group when the bar traversed the RF surround (Figure 2h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: GABAergic inputs onto SACs play an important role in generating motion-evoked surround suppression of SACs that transiently prevents visual noise-evoked SAC activation prior to their motion-evoked activation.
source: Therefore, GABAergic inputs onto SACs play an important role in generating motion-evoked surround suppression of SACs that transiently prevents visual noise-evoked SAC activation prior to their motion-evoked activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing impaired surround suppression in Gabra2 cKO mice.

claim: In Vgat cKO mice, only the SAC-SAC inhibition, but not the WAC-SAC inhibition, is impaired.
source: Unlike the Gabra2 cKO in which all GABAergic inputs to SACs are removed, only the SAC-SAC inhibition, but not the WAC-SAC inhibition, is impaired in the Vgat cKO mouse line (Figure 2c schematic).
evidence: This claim is based on the genetic manipulation described in the manuscript.

claim: Compared to the controls, SACs in Vgat cKO mice exhibited weaker surround suppression and enhanced flicker response before the motion response, a deficit similar to that observed in Gabra2 cKO mice.
source: We found that compared to the controls, SACs in Vgat cKO mice exhibited weaker surround suppression and enhanced flicker response before the motion response, a deficit similar to that observed in Gabra2 cKO mice (Figure 2b–i).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b-i.

claim: Weaker surround suppression was observed in the Vgat cKO and Gabra2 cKO groups during a contracting ring stimulus.
source: Weaker surround suppression was also observed in the Vgat cKO and Gabra2 cKO groups during a contracting ring stimulus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The strong SAC surround suppression evoked by the moving bar is mainly attributed to inhibitory inputs from neighboring SACs.
source: Therefore, we attribute the strong SAC surround suppression evoked by the moving bar mainly to inhibitory inputs from neighboring SACs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of Gabra2 cKO and Vgat cKO mice.

claim: Short-term depression at the SAC-DSGC GABAergic synapse has been demonstrated in P7-14 animals during development using paired pulse stimulation.
source: Short-term depression at the SAC-DSGC GABAergic synapse has been demonstrated in P7-14 animals during development using paired pulse stimulation (Morrie and Feller, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The IPSCs of DSGCs showed pronounced short-term depression in the paired pulse protocol in adult control mice.
source: The IPSCs of DSGCs showed pronounced short-term depression in the paired pulse protocol (Figure 3), indicating that the SAC-DSGC synapse is prone to depression by repeated SAC activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The SAC-DSGC synapse is prone to depression by repeated SAC activation.
source: The IPSCs of DSGCs showed pronounced short-term depression in the paired pulse protocol (Figure 3), indicating that the SAC-DSGC synapse is prone to depression by repeated SAC activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing short-term depression.

claim: The peak amplitudes of the somatic and distal dendritic Vm of SACs are comparable during a moving bar over the flickering checkerboard.
source: Simulation of SAC activation during a moving bar over the flickering checkerboard indicated that the peak amplitudes of the somatic and distal dendritic Vm are comparable (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The membrane depolarization at SAC dendritic tips is about 25% of somatic depolarization in the whole-cell voltage-clamp configuration.
source: Due to the electrotonic isolation of distal SAC dendrites from the soma (Euler et al., 2002; Koren et al., 2017; Tukker et al., 2004), we estimated the membrane depolarization at SAC dendritic tips by computational modeling to be about 25% of somatic depolarization in the whole-cell voltage-clamp configuration used in our study (Figure 4c).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling shown in Figure 4c and citations to prior research.

claim: Even though the SAC was activated by the same motion-evoked depolarization pattern, a more active Vm immediately before motion-evoked depolarization in the cKO waveform led to smaller DSGC IPSC peak amplitudes evoked by the motion waveform.
source: However, DSGC IPSCs triggered by the motion-evoked SAC waveforms (Figure 5a and b, time window 3) were significantly different between the cKO and the control patterns. Even though the SAC was activated by the same motion-evoked depolarization pattern during time window 3, a more active Vm immediately before motion-evoked depolarization (Figure 5a and b, time window 2) in the cKO waveform led to smaller DSGC IPSC peak amplitudes evoked by the motion waveform (Figure 5a–d, time window 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a-d.

claim: The synaptic suppression observed in the cKO group was robust when tested with additional scale factors of 3 and 5 for SAC command waveforms.
source: Furthermore, the synaptic suppression observed in the cKO group was robust when we tested additional scale factors of 3 and 5 for SAC command waveforms (Figure 5d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The duration of SAC surround suppression varies with motion speed.
source: Next, we recorded the SAC Vm during the moving bar stimuli at different speeds and examined the duration of surround suppression as a function of speed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5e and f.

claim: Speed-dependent duration of SAC surround suppression was observed in the sub-millisecond range over speeds of 110 µm/s, 440 µm/s, and 1320 µm/s.
source: As expected, we observed speed-dependent duration of SAC surround suppression in the sub-millisecond range over these speeds (Figure 5e and f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5e and f.

claim: For all three speeds tested, when random flickering checkerboard-evoked SAC activation fell in the SAC surround suppression time window, it could lead to reduced motion-evoked DSGC IPSCs.
source: We found that for all three speeds, when random flickering checkerboard-evoked SAC activation fell in the SAC surround suppression time window, it could lead to reduced motion-evoked DSGC IPSCs (Figure 5g and h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5g and h.

claim: In Gabra2 cKO mice, flicker-evoked SAC depolarization immediately preceding motion-evoked depolarization induces short-term depression at the SAC-DSGC GABAergic synapse, leading to reduced DSGC inhibition evoked by the moving bar.
source: Together, these results strongly support the hypothesis that in Gabra2 cKO mice, flicker-evoked SAC depolarization immediately preceding motion-evoked depolarization induces short-term depression at the SAC-DSGC GABAergic synapse, and thereby leads to reduced DSGC inhibition evoked by the moving bar.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from paired recordings and voltage clamp experiments.

claim: Synaptic depression attenuates the hyperpolarization of a SAC by its neighboring SACs in the presence of object motion with background noise.
source: Considering the extensive network of interconnected SACs (Ding et al., 2016; Lee and Zhou, 2006), one might ask whether synaptic depression attenuates the hyperpolarization of a SAC by its neighboring SACs in the presence of object motion with background noise. Consistent with this hypothesis, we did observe a weakened hyperpolarization of the SAC with the noisy background compared to the noise-free background (Figure 2e versus 2 hr).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e and 2h.

claim: Even though GABA release from SACs is depressed with a noisy background, object motion in the visual field still triggers sufficient GABA release from many neighboring SAC varicosities to suppress noise responses in the postsynaptic SAC just ahead of the moving object.
source: However, even though GABA release from SACs is depressed with a noisy background, object motion in the visual field still triggers sufficient GABA release from many neighboring SAC varicosities to suppress noise responses in the postsynaptic SAC just ahead of the moving object.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing surround suppression despite synaptic depression.

claim: The inverted algorithm of the SAC-SAC-DSGC disinhibitory motif arises from three mechanistic components: (1) lateral inhibition between neighboring SACs creates a SAC RF surround that is strongly engaged by visual motion, (2) a moving object entering the SAC RF surround transiently suppresses visual noise-evoked SAC activation prior to motion-evoked RF center response, and (3) the SAC-DSGC GABAergic synapse exhibits short-term synaptic depression on a timescale that matches that of visual noise-triggered network dynamics.
source: This computation arises from the concerted action of three mechanistic components (Figure 6): (1) The lateral inhibition between neighboring SACs creates a SAC RF surround that is strongly engaged by visual motion. (2) A moving object entering the SAC RF surround transiently suppresses visual noise-evoked SAC activation prior to motion-evoked RF center response; (3) The SAC-DSGC GABAergic synapse exhibits short-term synaptic depression on a timescale that matches that of visual noise-triggered network dynamics.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and computational modeling presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Visual motion stimuli across the center-surround RF elicit characteristic temporal activity profiles in visual neurons that can influence synaptic plasticity mechanisms.
source: Our findings highlight that visual motion stimuli across the center-surround RF elicit characteristic temporal activity profiles in visual neurons that can influence synaptic plasticity mechanisms.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental findings showing the interaction between SAC activation patterns and short-term depression.

claim: The modulation of short-term synaptic plasticity profoundly impacts the computational algorithm of the microcircuit in a context-dependent manner.
source: The modulation of short-term synaptic plasticity in turn profoundly impacts the computational algorithm of the microcircuit in a context-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental findings showing different circuit functions in noise-free versus noisy conditions.

claim: The SAC surround suppression provides a 'protective' time window to prevent noise-evoked activation from occurring immediately before motion-evoked activation in the SAC, which would otherwise depress its motion-evoked neurotransmitter release.
source: In this study, noise resilience is explored with a pattern of randomly flickering checkerboard that aims to effectively activate bipolar cells to feed 'noise' into the input end of the motion circuit in the IPL. While many other stimulus conditions await testing, the current set of experiments provides a mechanistic understanding of signal processing by this motif and indicates the SAC surround suppression provides a 'protective' time window to prevent noise-evoked activation from occurring immediately before motion-evoked activation in the SAC, which would otherwise depress its motion-evoked neurotransmitter release.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing the effects of surround suppression on synaptic depression.

claim: The protective function of SAC surround suppression does not necessitate that the SAC-DSGC synapse be chronically depressed by the baseline noise before the onset of motion-evoked surround suppression.
source: This function does not necessitate that the SAC-DSGC synapse be chronically depressed by the baseline noise before the onset of motion-evoked surround suppression.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing similar baseline IPSCs in control and cKO groups.

claim: The protective function of SAC surround suppression does not critically depend on the recovery from existing depression during the surround suppression window.
source: Therefore, this function does not critically depend on the recovery from existing depression during the surround suppression window.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data and the mechanism of the protective function.

claim: At higher speeds, the surround suppression window could be too short to separate the noise response from the motion response, so that synaptic depression could occur even with intact SAC-SAC inhibition in wild-type mice.
source: It is notable that the duration of SAC surround suppression varies with motion speed. At higher speeds, the surround suppression window could be too short to separate the noise response from the motion response, so that synaptic depression could occur even with intact SAC-SAC inhibition in wild-type mice.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning based on the observed speed-dependent duration of surround suppression.

claim: The more depressed motion-evoked release of Gabra2 cKO SACs is not only due to less recovery from synaptic depression, but is likely also due to further depression by the extra noise activity within the surround suppression window.
source: We reasoned that the more depressed motion-evoked release of Gabra2 cKO SACs is not only due to less recovery from synaptic depression, but is likely also due to further depression by the extra noise activity within the surround suppression window.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing synaptic depression with cKO waveforms.

claim: The SAC-SAC inhibition is effective in shielding the SAC from further depression by noise activity within the ~150 ms window prior to the motion response.
source: When we selected Gabra2 cKO SAC voltage traces that contained the 'unwanted' noise activation within this shorter window as command waveforms in paired recordings (Figure 5g, lower panel), we observed more severe synaptic depression of the SAC-DSGC synapse than with the control waveform. Therefore, the SAC-SAC inhibition is still effective in shielding the SAC from further depression by noise activity within the ~150 ms window prior to the motion response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5g.

claim: The short period immediately before the motion response plays an important role in shaping the motion-evoked SAC transmitter release.
source: The persistence of the protective role of SAC-SAC inhibition at the higher speed suggests that the short period immediately before the motion response plays an important role in shaping the motion-evoked SAC transmitter release.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing the effects of the surround suppression window.

claim: In the Off pathway, the SAC-SAC-DSGC motif is present.
source: In this study, we focused on the On pathway of the direction-selective circuit, which depends on the synaptic interactions between On SACs and the On dendritic layer of the bistratified On-Off DSGCs. In the Off pathway, the SAC-SAC-DSGC motif is also present (Ding et al., 2016), and may play a similar role in preserving DSGC direction selectivity under noisy conditions as in the On pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The SAC-SAC-DSGC motif in the Off pathway may play a similar role in preserving DSGC direction selectivity under noisy conditions as in the On pathway.
source: In the Off pathway, the SAC-SAC-DSGC motif is also present (Ding et al., 2016), and may play a similar role in preserving DSGC direction selectivity under noisy conditions as in the On pathway.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning based on the findings in the On pathway.

claim: Eliminating inhibitory inputs onto Off SACs in Gabra2 cKO mice leads to impaired direction selectivity of DSGCs even in the absence of visual noise in the background.
source: However, eliminating inhibitory inputs onto Off SACs in Gabra2 cKO mice leads to impaired direction selectivity of DSGCs even in the absence of visual noise in the background (Chen et al., 2016), making it difficult to unambiguously separate the roles of lateral inhibition motifs in the generation versus the noise resilience of direction selectivity in the Off pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Different functional contributions of anatomically symmetric motifs for the direction-selective responses to bright and dark motion stimuli suggest context-dependent neural computations by the 'hardwired' retinal circuitry.
source: Different functional contributions of anatomically symmetric motifs for the direction-selective responses to bright and dark motion stimuli suggest context-dependent neural computations by the 'hardwired' retinal circuitry.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differences observed between On and Off pathways.

claim: Wide-field amacrine cells contribute to the surround inhibition of SACs.
source: In addition to the inhibition from neighboring SACs, wide-field amacrine cells also contribute to the surround inhibition of SACs (Ding et al., 2016; Lee and Zhou, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In the absence of SAC-SAC inhibition in Vgat cKO mice, wide-field inhibition of the SAC was not strong enough to significantly suppress the noise response of the SAC in the noisy bar stimulus.
source: We found that in the absence of SAC-SAC inhibition in Vgat cKO mice, wide-field inhibition of the SAC was not strong enough to significantly suppress the noise response of the SAC in our noisy bar stimulus that was presented to a retinal area of 660 um in diameter.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Vgat cKO mice.

claim: More extensive stimuli may trigger stronger wide-field inhibition to further facilitate noise suppression.
source: It is possible that more extensive stimuli may trigger stronger wide-field inhibition to further facilitate noise suppression.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning about potential effects of different stimuli.

claim: Wide-field inhibition of SACs is sensitive to the continuity of moving edges, and thereby confers contextual modulation of pDSGC spiking response to compound gratings that differ between center and surround regions.
source: It has been shown that the wide-field inhibition of SACs is sensitive to the continuity of moving edges, and thereby confers contextual modulation of pDSGC spiking response to compound gratings that differ between center and surround regions (Huang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Wide-field amacrine cell inputs to SACs might mainly serve a function of detecting discontinuities while the SAC-SAC inhibition mediates strong surround suppression prior to the approaching motion.
source: Therefore, wide-field amacrine cell inputs to SACs might mainly serve a different function of detecting discontinuities while the SAC-SAC inhibition mediates strong surround suppression prior to the approaching motion.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data and prior research on wide-field inhibition.

claim: Surround suppression of inhibitory neurons by lateral inhibition is widely observed in both retinal and cortical circuits.
source: The mechanistic components underlying the inverted role of disinhibition in our study are broadly relevant to brain circuitry within and beyond the retina. For example, surround suppression of inhibitory neurons by lateral inhibition is widely observed in both retinal [Eggers and Lukasiewicz, 2010) and cortical circuits (e.g. (Ayaz et al., 2013; Fu et al., 2014; Pecka et al., 2014; Pi et al., 2013]).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The prevalence of disinhibitory motifs, synaptic plasticity at multiple time scales, and context-dependent network dynamics raises the possibility that this motif can implement a richer set of neural computations beyond disinhibition in other brain regions such as cortex and hippocampus.
source: The prevalence of disinhibitory motifs, synaptic plasticity at multiple time scales, and context-dependent network dynamics raises the possibility that this motif can implement a richer set of neural computations beyond disinhibition in other brain regions such as cortex and hippocampus (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning based on the findings and citation to prior research.

claim: VIP+ interneurons inhibit other inhibitory neurons in the neocortex and hippocampus and play important roles in gating and gain control during sensory and cognitive processing.
source: For example, vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) + interneurons, which are known to inhibit other inhibitory neurons in the neocortex and hippocampus, have been shown to play important roles in gating and gain control during sensory and cognitive processing.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge about VIP interneurons.

claim: The VIP interneuron-mediated motif is subject to the same influence of ongoing network activity and short-term plasticity as the SAC-mediated motif, and therefore is likely susceptible to similar algorithmic flexibility.
source: Although the VIP interneuron-mediated disinhibitory motif differs from the SAC-mediated motif in many specific aspects such as cellular physiology, embedded networks, and input signals, the VIP interneuron-mediated motif is subject to the same influence of ongoing network activity and short-term plasticity, and therefore is likely susceptible to similar algorithmic flexibility as depicted mechanistically in the current study.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning based on the findings in the retina.

claim: Context-dependent computation is likely a general property of microcircuit motifs in the brain because synaptic plasticity and network activity patterns are universal and fundamental elements of brain circuits that exert mutual influences onto each other.
source: We further postulate that context-dependent computation is likely a general property of microcircuit motifs in the brain because synaptic plasticity and network activity patterns are universal and fundamental elements of brain circuits that exert mutual influences onto each other.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning based on the findings and general principles of neuroscience.

claim: Future studies that explore the interplay between synaptic plasticity and network dynamics in circuit analysis and modeling will improve our understanding and prediction of the input-output relationships of diverse brain circuits.
source: Future studies that explore the interplay between synaptic plasticity and network dynamics in circuit analysis and modeling will improve our understanding and prediction of the input-output relationships of diverse brain circuits.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning about future research directions.

claim: Mice from postnatal 21 to 60 days were used in the experiments.
source: Mice from postnatal 21 to 60 days were used in the experiments.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the experimental subjects.

claim: The intensity of the moving bar was ~6.3×10^4 isomerizations (R*)/rod/s, in the photopic range.
source: The intensity of the moving bar was ~6.3×104 isomerizations (R*)/rod/s, in the photopic range.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the visual stimulus.

claim: For the noise-free background, the intensity of background was ~1800 R*/rod/s, at the lower end of photopic range.
source: For the noise-free background, the intensity of background was ~1800 R*/rod/s, at the lower end of photopic range.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the visual stimulus.

claim: For the noisy background, individual checks were 55 µm x 55 µm in size, with intensity at either background (0) or ~1×10^4 R*/rod/s drawn from a binomial distribution.
source: For the noisy background, the noise was generated as a randomly flickering checkerboard. Individual checks were 55 µm x 55 µm in size, with intensity at either background (0) or ~1×104 R*/rod/s drawn from a binomial distribution.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the visual stimulus.

claim: The checkerboard pattern was refreshed at 15 Hz.
source: The checkerboard pattern was refreshed at 15 Hz.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the visual stimulus.

claim: Space clamp is an intrinsic limitation of the voltage clamp method.
source: Space clamp is an intrinsic limitation of the voltage clamp method.
evidence: This is established knowledge about electrophysiological methods.

claim: Light-evoked EPSCs and IPSCs of DSGCs measured by somatic voltage clamp recordings have been taken to well approximate at least the proximal synaptic inputs based on pharmacological and conductance analysis.
source: While space clamp is still an issue at distal dendrites (Percival et al., 2019; Poleg-Polsky and Diamond, 2011), light-evoked EPSCs and IPSCs of DSGCs measured by somatic voltage clamp recordings have been taken to well approximate at least the proximal synaptic inputs based on pharmacological and conductance analysis (e.g. (Cafaro and Rieke, 2010; Taylor and Vaney, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.
